headline: Welcome to the live coverage of stage 12 of La Vuelta 26
subtext: Back to the mountains - as La Vuelta 26 settles in Almeria, the peloton face a gruelling 4,568 metres of elevation gain between Vera and the summit finish at Calar Alto, past the Alto de Velefique. The neutral start is set at 13:00, the start proper at 13:07 after a 2.3 km parade, and the winners should be crowned at around 17:30.

headline: Welcome to Almeria
subtext: Today’s stage is entirely set in the province of Almeria, visited by La Vuelta for the first time since Kaden Groves won in Cabo de Gata in 2022. Cristian Rodríguez (XDS Astana) is the local rider of the day as he hails from El Ejido, near Almeria, around 100 kilometres from today’s course. The main local cycling event is the Clasica de Almeria, held since 1986 and won by Biniam Girmay last February. Magnus Cort won it in 2017. The women’s event has been held since 2023. The first edition finished in Vera - Canada’s Emilie Fortin won ahead of her compatriot Alison Jackson.

headline: An unprecedented start… where Hayter already built sweet memories
subtext: Vera make its debut as La Vuelta stage town*. Ethan Hayter won the final stage of the 2021 Vuelta a Andalucia, starting in Vera. *The full list of new stage towns in this edition: Monaco (stage 1), Manosque (2), Font-Romeu (stage 3), Falset (5), Roquetes (5), Vall d’Alba (7), Puçol (8), Xeraco (8), La Vila Joiosa (9), Alcaraz (10), Elche de la Sierra (10), Vera (12), Almuñécar (13), Palma del Rio (15), Cortegana (16), La Rábida (16), Dos Hermanas (17), El Puerto de Santa María (18), La Calahorra (20), and Collado del Aguacil (20).

headline: Brennan in the footsteps of Pogacar, Gaviria and Sagan
subtext: A few weeks after his 21st birthday, Matthew Brennan (Visma-Lease a Bike) already has three Grand Tour stage wins under his belt. He is the first Grand Tour debutant with three stage wins since Tadej Pogacar in La Vuelta 19. He is the first sprinter to claim three stage wins in his maiden Grand Tour since Fernando Gaviria in the Giro 2017. The Colombian even pushed his tally to four wins on that occasion. And he continues to fuel the comparisons with Peter Sagan, who won three stages in his first Grand Tour, La Vuelta 11.

headline: 3 non-starters
subtext: There are 163 riders in the absence of Ben Tulett (Visma-Lease a Bike), David Gonzalez (Pinarello Q36.5) and Lindsay De Vylder (Alpecin-Premier Tech).

headline: Let’s roll
subtext: The peloton make their way to the start proper with a 2.3 km parade.

headline: La Roja
subtext: Enric Mas (Movistar) faces another key challenge in his bid to defend La Roja just a few days after his dominant display at Alto de Aitana. Can he also make the most of the sequence with Alto de Velefique and Calar Alto? The Spaniard starts the day with a gap of 1’18’’ to Primoz Roglic (Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe) and 1’39’’ to Felix Gall (Decathlon CMA CGM). Oscar Onley (Netcompany Ineos) is fourth, trailing by 2’20’’.

headline: Green jersey
subtext: With a top 5 result yesterday while leading out Matthew Brennan to victory, Wout van Aert maintained the lead of the points standings (174 points) ahead of his British teammate (117 points). Alessandro Romele (XDS Astana) is third with 96 pointes, two more than Bryan Coquard (Cofidis).

headline: Polka dot jersey
subtext: After he was second at the Alto de Aledo yesterday, Santiago Buitrago (Bahrain Victorious) is up to 31 KOM points, seven more than Enric Mas (Movistar). Wout van Aert (Visma-Lease a Bike) sprinted ahead of the Colombian climber to take 3 points and bring his tally up to 19 points, as many as Andreas Leknessund (Uno-X Mobility).

headline: White jersey
subtext: Oscar Onley (Netcompany Ineos) is still 5’45’’ ahead of Jakob Omrzel (Bahrain Victorious), while Jarno Widar (Lotto Intermarché) trails by 7’14’’.

headline: Team standings
subtext: With Alessandro Romele (8th), Henok Mulubrhan (13th) and Harold Tejada (24th) in the mix yesterday, XDS Astana had the best collective performance in Lorca, but Decathlon CMA CGM retained the lead of the overall team standings ahead of Netcompany Ineos (42’’55’’) and Visma-Lease a Bike (50’12’’).

headline: Combativity award
subtext: Ethan Hayter (Soudal Quick-Step) will race with a distinctive bib again as he was named the most combative rider for the third time (stages 2, 5 and 11).

headline: Stage 12 is ON!
subtext: The 163-man peloton passed km 0 and can battle it out on a most demanding stage!

headline: Ethan Hayter is the first attacker of the day
subtext: There are many contenders for today's breakaway.

headline: An intense start

headline: On the first climb of the day
Van Aert gets in the mix

2 more riders in the breakaway

subtext: +1'15'' Sivakov +4'15'' Peloton

headline: No direct threat for Mas, but some GC contenders at the front
subtext: The gap from the 30 leaders to the peloton is up to 5 minutes. There are four riders from the GC top 20 in the breakaway: - Jakob Omrzel (Bahrain Victorious), 10th with a gap of 8'05'', also 2nd of the best young riders standings 5'45'' behind Onley; - Léo Bisiaux (Decathlon CMA CGM), 15th, +13'51'' - Ramses Debruyne (Alpecin-Premier Tech), 18th, +23'23'' - Finlay Pickering (Jayco AlUla), 20th, +24'43''

subtext: Almeida, Van Aert, Bisiaux, Buitrago, Lutsenko and Kron attack ahead of the third climb of the day, but their breakaway rivals react.

headline: 100 kilometres to go

headline: The 3rd climb of the day
subtext: The attackers tackle 18.5 km of ascent on irregular slopes to reach the Collado Garcia (cat. 2).

headline: Canal and Arcas take turns for Mas: "Enric is full of confidence"
subtext: Jorge Arcas (Movistar) spoke at the start about his role as a domestique for Enric Mas: “Yes, the truth is that this is a very good stage for Enric [Mas]. As I always say, I’ve been with Enric for many years. I’ve always had complete confidence in him. I’m a domestique who’s always as close to him as possible. He’s been through some tough times, and for me it’s a privilege to be able to defend the red jersey. That’s what I do best: working for my team. I reckon Enric is going to have a good stage today, and we’re going to try to be right up there with the best. I think Enric is in exceptional form right now, and we’re going to fight to extend the lead, I hope. He looks very good to me, and above all, he’s full of confidence.”

headline: The peloton begin the ascent
subtext: The gap at the bottom: 5'35''.

headline: Uno-X Mobility invest in the break: "Tobias Johannessen deserves to have a stage win"
subtext: Andreas Leknessund spoke about Uno-X Mobility's will to have several riders around Tobias Johannessen in today's break: "I still have to work a bit, yesterday we were expecting an easy day but with the temperatures it has become quite hard. We still need to focus and we really want to have a new stage win. I think [Tobias Johannessen] deserves to have a stage win so I really want to help him with that, this stage is probably not for me but the first part can be good for me so I should try. [We need] to have him in the breakaway and hopefully with one more from the team so we can maintain a high speed, we want the breakaway to go as early as possible because then you get a bigger gap. We just need to be at the front from the start and hope for a strong group to go. And if not, we’ll look for the next days."

headline: La Vuelta stage winners in the breakaway
subtext: Three years ago today, on 3 September 2023, Lennard Kamna (Lidl-Trek) won at Collado de la Cruz de Caravaca a stage that started in Cartagena (yesterday's start town). The other stage winners in the breakaway are: - Wout van Aert (Visma-Lease a Bike) : Castelo Branco 2024, Cordoba 2024, Baiona 2024 - Pablo Castrillo (Movistar) : Estacion de Montana de Manzaneda 2024, Valgrande-Pajares.Cuitu Negru 2024 - Eddie Dunbar (Pinarello-Q36.5) : Campus Tecnologico Cortizo Padron 2024, Picon Blanco 2024 - Joao Almeida (UAE Emirates XRG) : L'Angliru 2025 - Urko Berrade (Kern Pharma) : Maestru-Parque Natural de Izki 2024 - Andreas Kron (Uno-X Mobility) : Barcelona 2023 - Andreas Leknessund (Uno-X Mobility) : Aramon Valdelinares 2026 - Alexey Lutsenko (NSN) : Alcossebre 2017

headline: The average speed after 2 hours: 39.1 km/h
subtext: The leaders maintain a strong pace and keep extending their lead: 5'57''.

headline: Bilbao: “Santiago is in brilliant form”
subtext: Riding at the front today, Pello Bilbao (Bahrain Victorious) has already won stages of the Tour de France and the Giro d’Italia, but never in La Vuelta. This is his last Grand Tour before retiring. “Of course [I’d like to secure a stage win in La Vuelta to complete my victories in all three Grand Tours], but I wouldn’t say I’m going to go mad about it either”, the Basque climber said today at the start. “I don’t want to become obsessed with this goal and neglect the work I’m doing for the team, which I believe is key. We’ve got several objectives on the table; every day we want to fight for the best possible stage result, and we’ll see how it goes. If my chance comes, I’ll try not to let it slip.” Bilbao already worked in breakaways for Buitrago and he seems to play a similar part so far today. “We know Santiago is in brilliant form”, Bilbao said. “He’s surely the strongest rider to win this mountains classification, and he’s also in with a chance of winning a stage.”

headline: Omrzel takes the virtual white jersey
subtext: With a gap of 6 minutes from the breakaway to the peloton, Jakob Omrzel (Bahrain Victorious) moves the 4th place in the virtual overall standings, ahead of Oscar Onley (Netcompany Ineos). The young Slovenian needs 6'26'' to move past Primoz Roglic (Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe) in the third place.

headline: Van Aert also takes the 3rd summit of the day
subtext: Buitrago tried to anticipate, but he was second again.

headline: The battle for the polka dot jersey is in full swing
subtext: Wout van Aert (Visma-Lease a Bike) went first atop the first three categorised climbs on the day, with Santiago Buitrago (Bahrain Victorious) in second position. The Colombian wearer of the polka dot jersey still leads the mountains standings with a tally of 38 points. The Belgian star is now in second position with 30 points. Enric Mas still has 24 points.

headline: The gap has increased on the climb
subtext: The peloton crest the ascent with the biggest gap so far today: 6'35''.

headline: The attackers are back on the valley
subtext: Wout van Aert (Visma-Lease a Bike) and Santiago Buitrago (Bahrain Victorious) are caught after opening a gap of 20 seconds on the downhill.

headline: Memories from Alto de Velefique and Calar Alto
subtext: Alto de Velefique was introduced in La Vuelta 2004, en route to the first summit finish at Calar Alto. It has been passed in every stage finishing at Calar Alto (2004, 2006, 2017) and was also the setting of two summit finishes in 2009 and 2021. On the last occasion, Damiano Caruso took the stage winter a 71-km solo attack. Wearing La Roja, Primoz Roglic was second at the summit ahead of Enric Mas, the runner-up in the overall standings.Among the participants of La Vuelta 26 who climbed Calar Alto in 2017, David de la Cruz had the best result (10th) while Enric Mas finished 115th. “I was sick”, he recalled yesterday. De la Cruz and Mas were teammates at Quick-Step Floors that year.

headline: De la Cruz: "Calar Alto is a very uneven climb"
subtext: David de la Cruz (Pinarello-Q36.5) was 10th at Calar Alto in 2017 and he described the challenges before today’s stage: "I have bittersweet memories because, to be honest, my legs felt really strong that day but I had a mechanical problem right at the start of the climb, which meant I couldn’t fight for the win. It’s a very uneven climb. The first section is very tough; the first 5 kilometres are almost 10%, and you’re coming straight down from Velefique. Then, the second section of the climb is much more uneven, more like a series of steps. I remember that the upper section before reaching the Observatory was a narrower road with very poor tarmac. Ultimately, it’s a climb where you have to survive the first section if you’re in contention for the stage, and then, on the more favourable part, play your cards right or go for it in the sprint."

headline: Omrzel stands on the virtual GC podium
subtext: The peloton reach km 104 with a gap of 6'40''. The Slovenian youngster trailed by 8'05'' at the start of the stage.

headline: The toughest break of this race so far
Brenner: "I'm confident it will be a breakaway day"
subtext: Marco Brenner (Tudor) had a huge smile at the start. And the race dynamics are currently going his way: “Today will be a super hard day. I think it can be a breakaway day, so I look forward to today. So far, we didn’t see many days for the breakaway, so I think today can be an opportunity. You never know for 100%, but it looks like there’s this chance for the breakaway. I’m actually confident it will be a breakaway day. I think you can see it’s a different way of controlling the race, if you compare to UAE Team Emirates before and now it’s Movistar with the leader’s jersey. I think they go a little bit back to the old school way of controlling the race, so I expect, with the harder stages coming, there will be more opportunities for the breakaway to arrive to the finish.”

headline: 7 minutes
subtext: The attackers are working hard on the valley leading to Velefique. They will soon enter the final 50 kilometres. Pello Bilbao (Bahrain Victorious) returns to the front group after a mechanical.

headline: 5 kilometres to the intermediate sprint
subtext: Wout van Aert (Visma-Lease a Bike) will also aim for this line, in addition to the summits he's already conquered.

headline: Up the Alto de Velefique
subtext: The attackers tackle the first cat. 1 ascent of the day: 13.1 km at 7.2%. They're about to pass the intermediate sprint. The last gap to the peloton: 7'28''.

headline: Van Aert also takes the intermediate sprint
subtext: Oliveira, Kämna and Hamilton have been dropped.

headline: Van Aert sits up
subtext: The Belgian all rounder has taken 13 KOM points and 20 points for the green jersey.

headline: Almeida pulls the breakaway
subtext: Vermaerke is on his wheel.

subtext: 1. Van Aert, 20 pts 2. Almeida, 17 pts 3. Vermaerke, 15 pts 4. Kron, 13 pts 5. Rochas, 10 pts

headline: 2 Movistar riders in the peloton: Romeo and Mas
subtext: Aular has just been dropped. Castrillo and Garcia Pierna are in the breakaway, 7'30'' ahead of the peloton.

headline: 40 kilometres to go
subtext: Almeida, Vermaerke, Buitrago, Bisiaux, Lutsenko, Omrzel, Tuckwell, Berrade, Pickering, Haig, Garcia Pierna, Castrillo are at the front while Johannessen drops to his team car. Their average speed after three hours: 41.1 km/h.

subtext: Buitrago is on his wheel and Bisiaux is quick to react as they tackle the final 9 kilometres up the Alto de Velefique. Lutsenko rapidly joins them. Tuckwell drives the chase behind them.

headline: Carapaz attacks from far away
subtext: The Ecuadorian climber came from behind and went all in! He is about 39 km from the finish.

headline: Carapaz has opened a 15-second gap
subtext: The Ecuadorian climber has passed Oliveira and Van Aert. Romeo sets the pace in the bunch.

headline: Castrillo is dropped from the lead group
subtext: The Spaniard is likely waiting for the GC group to help Enric Mas. Carapaz is now 20 seconds ahead of the GC group.

subtext: Meanwhile, the attackers are inside the final kilometre of ascent.

subtext: Omrzel and Bisiaux were caught just before the summit.

headline: 20 kilometres to go for the leaders
subtext: At the same time, the GC group enter the final 25 kilometres with a gap of 5'10''.

headline: The highest summit finish of La Vuelta 26
subtext: At 2,153 metres, Calar Alto is the highest summit finish of La Vuelta 26. Last year, stage 20 finished at 2,251 metres (Bola del Mundo). Jonas Vingegaard was the winner to seal his overall victory. Passed on stage 4 as the race headed to Andorra La Vella, Port d’Envalira (2,409m) was the other 2000+ summit of the 2026 edition. Today’s route makes for the third stage with the highest elevation gain in La Vuelta 26: - stage 9, La Vila Joiosa > Alto de Aitana, 5,166 m - stage 20, La Calahorra > Collado del Alguacil, 4,890 m - stage 12, Vera > Calar Alto, 4,568 m

headline: Onto the final climb: Calar Alto!
subtext: These are the nine leaders at the bottom of the 16.9 km ascent: Tuckwell, Garcia Pierna, Bisiaux, Haig, Buitrago, Omrzel, Lutsenko, Vansevenant and Berrade.

subtext: Garcia Pierna and then Vansevenant are dropped. The last gap to the bunch: 5'15''.

subtext: Only Berrade follows. Bisiaux tries to chase them.

headline: Omrzel goes solo with 12 km to go
subtext: Berrade can't keep up anymore.
